plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks crowned with enormous golden faces that follow the sun across the sky, filling Great Plains fields and farm gardens with a blaze of yellow around a dark, seed-packed center.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn, typically July through September in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Central and eastern United States, including the Great Plains
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds track the sun from east to west during the day, then swing back toward the east overnight. Mature blooms stop moving and permanently face east.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: Wind-swept moorlands turn into rolling carpets of purple as countless tiny bell-shaped blooms open across the wiry, evergreen shrubs. The hills hum with foraging bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer into autumn, roughly August through October
plants.location: Moorlands and heathlands of Scotland and northern England
plants.funFact: Heather honey is prized for its thick, jelly-like texture, and beekeepers often move their hives onto the moors in August to catch the bloom.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Southern Australia's national floral emblem bursts into fluffy golden pom-poms that perfume the bush with a honeyed fragrance. It is a bright sign that winter is turning toward spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, roughly July through September in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Australians celebrate National Wattle Day on September 1, and the golden wattle's green and gold colors inspired the country's national sporting colors.
